snapshots.title: Massachusetts cities and towns with county and DPH preparedness region
snapshots.publisher: MassGIS (Bureau of Geographic Information); region assignment derived by this project
snapshots.license: MassGIS data are free public records of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts.
snapshots.derivation: Town, type, county, and county FIPS come from the MassGIS municipal boundary layer (TOWNSSURVEY_POLY). Each town's DPH Emergency Preparedness Region is the region polygon (REGDPHEP_POLY) that contains an interior point of the town's largest land part. The HMCC region merges DPH Regions 4A and 4B into 4AB, then applies the towns whose region differs on DPH's HMCC Regional Boundaries map (MDPH OPEM, 2019-12-09; PDF retrieved 2026-11-07, not re-downloaded by the build): Wilmington (Region 3).
caveats: The DPH Emergency Preparedness Region layer dates from 2005. HMCC membership is derived from it (Regions 4A and 4B merged into 4AB) and was compared town by town with DPH's HMCC Regional Boundaries map (December 2019) on 2026-11-07; the towns that differ are set to the map's region: Wilmington (Region 3). DPH's interactive HMCC locator could not be checked. Confirm with your HMCC.

snapshots.title: Massachusetts public school districts (academic, charter, and vocational)
snapshots.publisher: MassGIS, from Massachusetts DESE district data
snapshots.license: MassGIS data are free public records of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts.
snapshots.derivation: Districts from SCHOOLDISTRICTS_POLY (municipal and regional academic) plus charter and vocational-technical districts from SCHOOLDISTRICTS_CCUV_POLY, keyed by DESE 8-digit organization code.
caveats: District boundaries and membership reflect the MassGIS layer's vintage; districts formed, merged, or renamed since then are missing. Confirm with DESE School and District Profiles.

snapshots.title: CDC IIS vaccine code sets: CVX, MVX, product trade names, and vaccine NDCs
snapshots.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, National Center for Immunization and Respiratory Diseases
snapshots.source_vintage: code sets as published 2026-11-07 (NDC page last reviewed 2026-09-18)
snapshots.derivation: Pipe-delimited flat files converted to CSV with headers; whitespace trimmed; numeric CVX codes zero-padded to two digits; dates normalized to YYYY-MM-DD. NDC tables keep the NDC11 (dashed), level (unit of sale or unit of use), proprietary name, labeler, start and end dates, packaging, route, and CVX; generic names and GTINs were dropped to keep the file small. Rebuild with the same conversion from the source URLs. Builder: xtask/scripts/build_cvx.py (run with Python 3 on the downloaded flat files).
caveats: CDC updates these code sets whenever products are licensed, renamed, or discontinued; the tool tries the live CVX file first and falls back to this snapshot.
CDC notes that some GTINs in its NDC tables were inaccurate; GTINs are not included here.

snapshots.title: Massachusetts school immunization survey results by school (kindergarten and grade 7, 2025-2026; kindergarten 2023-2026 combined)
snapshots.publisher: Massachusetts Department of Public Health, Immunization Division
snapshots.source_vintage: 2025-2026 school year (data current as of April 5, 2026 per DPH)
snapshots.license: Public records of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts.
snapshots.derivation: The 'Rates by School' sheet of each DPH workbook, one row per school. Rates published as fractions (0.91) are stored as whole percents (91). DPH's markers become a status column: dagger (fewer than 30 students; DPH does not release rates) -> suppressed_lt30, asterisk (no survey returned) -> no_response, pilcrow (unresolved discrepancy) -> discrepancy, N/A (survey returned with zero students) -> no_students. Kindergarten columns: 5 DTaP, 4 polio, 2 MMR, 3 HepB, 2 varicella, series complete, exemption, unimmunized (exemption with no vaccines), no record, non-compliance. Grade 7 columns: 2 MMR, 3 HepB, 2 varicella, 1 Tdap, 1 MenACWY, series, exemption, unimmunized, no record, non-compliance. Builder: xtask/scripts/build_school_survey.py (Python 3 with openpyxl).
caveats: Self-reported by schools; DPH notes discrepancies may exist and rates can change during the year.
DPH publishes rates only (no enrollment counts) and withholds schools with fewer than 30 students; the 3-year combined kindergarten file releases schools whose pooled count reaches 30.
Exemption rates combine medical and religious exemptions.

snapshots.title: Vaccination coverage for Massachusetts and the United States (NIS-Child, NIS-Teen, FluVaxView, SchoolVaxView kindergarten)
snapshots.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (National Immunization Surveys; VaxView)
snapshots.source_vintage: NIS-Child birth years 2018-2022 (rows updated 2026-04-02); NIS-Teen 2020-2025 (2026-09-03); influenza seasons 2021-22 to 2025-26, May estimates (2026-10-08); kindergarten 2021-22 to 2025-26 (2026-08-28)
snapshots.derivation: SoQL queries for geography in ('Massachusetts','United States'): NIS-Child dimension_type 'Age' and dimension '24 Months' or '35 Months'; NIS-Teen dimension '13-17 Years'; influenza dimension_type 'Age', month 5 (end-of-season cumulative estimate); kindergarten all vaccines and exemptions. Columns kept: survey, dataset, vaccine, dose, geography, period, group, coverage_pct, ci_95, sample_size, exemptions. Builder: xtask/scripts/build_nis.py (Python 3 standard library; prints each query URL).
caveats: Survey estimates have sampling error; compare confidence intervals, not point estimates alone. State estimates with small samples are flagged by CDC.
NIS-Child reports by birth year, so the most recent cohort lags several years behind the calendar.
Federal datasets were modified or paused at times in 2025-2026; check the data date before citing.

snapshots.title: Massachusetts census geographies: counties, cities and towns (county subdivisions), 2020 census tracts, and ZCTAs, with crosswalks
snapshots.publisher: U.S. Census Bureau; crosswalk derived by this project
snapshots.derivation: Towns: the 351 Massachusetts county subdivisions in the 2024 Census Gazetteer, matched to MassGIS town names (Census suffixes such as 'city', 'town', and 'Town city' removed). Tracts: 2020 census tracts; the town of each tract and its share come from the 2020 block assignment file (share of the tract's census blocks in each town). ZCTAs: 2020 ZCTAs that overlap a Massachusetts town in the 2020 ZCTA-to-county-subdivision relationship file; town shares are shares of the ZCTA's land area. PUMAs: 2020 tract-to-PUMA relationship file. Land area in square miles from the Gazetteer.
caveats: Tract-to-town shares count census blocks, not people; a few tracts cross town lines.
ZIP Code Tabulation Areas approximate USPS ZIP Codes and often cross town lines; town shares are by land area.

snapshots.title: Massachusetts map boundaries: cities and towns, 2020 census tracts, ZCTAs, and school districts
snapshots.publisher: U.S. Census Bureau cartographic boundary files; school districts derived by this project
snapshots.derivation: Polygons from the 1:500,000 cartographic boundary files (clipped to the shoreline), projected to NAD83 / Massachusetts Mainland (EPSG:26986), simplified with Douglas–Peucker (tolerance 60 m for towns and school districts, 25 m for tracts, 50 m for ZCTAs) with shared borders simplified identically, quantized to 10 m, and delta-encoded (polygons separated by '|', rings by ';', 'x y dx dy ...' in 10 m units). School districts (municipal, regional academic, and regional vocational-technical; DESE organization codes from the MassGIS district list) are the union of their member towns.
caveats: Boundaries are simplified for maps at town to state scale and are not survey-grade.
Regional secondary and vocational districts overlap the elementary or municipal districts of their member towns.
School district membership follows the 2019 MassGIS district list; newer regionalizations are missing.

snapshots.title: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 2020–2024 5-year estimates (detailed tables)
snapshots.derivation: From the ACS 5-year table-based summary file: every cell an indicator needs, for the nation, Massachusetts, its 14 counties, 351 county subdivisions (cities and towns), and populated 2020 census tracts. Indicators are sums and percentages of detailed-table cells (definitions in phn_data::census::INDICATORS, with table IDs). Margins of error (90%) of sums use sqrt(sum of squared MOEs), counting only the largest MOE among zero estimates; percentages use the Census Bureau's derived-proportion formula (ratio formula when the radicand is negative). Counts and dollars are rounded to whole numbers, percentages to one decimal. ma_acs5_languages_detailed.csv holds B16001 detailed languages (speakers and those who speak English less than 'very well') for Massachusetts and its 2020 PUMAs, the smallest areas where B16001 is published.
caveats: ACS 5-year estimates describe the five-year period, not a single year, and carry sampling error; check the margin of error and coefficient of variation before comparing areas.
Small towns and tracts have large margins of error; estimates with a coefficient of variation above 30% are flagged as unreliable.
Dollar amounts are in inflation-adjusted dollars of the last year of the period.

snapshots.title: CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index 2022, Massachusetts census tracts
snapshots.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention / Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry, Geospatial Research, Analysis, and Services Program
snapshots.derivation: Massachusetts tracts from the state-ranked file (percentile ranks within Massachusetts, columns ma_rpl_*) joined to the same tracts in the U.S.-ranked file (national percentile ranks, us_rpl_*). Kept: total population and MOE, overall and four theme percentile ranks, the count of flags (F_TOTAL, tracts at or above the 90th percentile on a variable), and the 16 percent estimates (EP_*). -999 (no data) is stored as blank.
caveats: SVI ranks are relative (percentiles); they do not measure absolute need and cannot be compared across SVI releases.
Rankings within Massachusetts and nationally differ; say which one you use.
Built from ACS 2018–2022 5-year estimates, which have sampling error at the tract level.

snapshots.title: CDC PLACES: Local Data for Better Health, 2025 release (Massachusetts counties, places, census tracts, and ZCTAs)
snapshots.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Division of Population Health
snapshots.source_vintage: PLACES 2025 release (BRFSS 2023 for 35 measures, 2022 for 5; ACS 2019–2023 or 2018–2022)
snapshots.derivation: Rows for Massachusetts from the four PLACES 2025 datasets on data.cdc.gov (county swc5-untb, place eav7-hnsx, tract cwsq-ngmh, ZCTA qnzd-25i4), reshaped to one row per location and estimate type (crude, and for counties and places also age-adjusted) with each measure's estimate and 95% confidence limits. ZCTAs and tracts are limited to those in ma_census_geographies.csv. ma_places_2025_measures.csv lists each measure's name, category, and BRFSS data year, with U.S. and Massachusetts reference values computed by this project as adult-population-weighted means of county estimates (sum of estimate × population 18+ over sum of population 18+), which are not official CDC state estimates and have no confidence interval.
caveats: PLACES estimates are model-based small-area estimates, not direct survey measurements; CDC cautions against using them to evaluate local programs or policies.
The data year (BRFSS survey year) differs from the release year.
U.S. and Massachusetts reference values are population-weighted means of county estimates computed by this server, not official CDC state estimates.

snapshots.title: NNDSS Weekly Data: Massachusetts, New England, and U.S. residents
snapshots.publisher: CDC, Office of Public Health Data, Surveillance, and Technology
snapshots.license: U.S. federal government work (CDC open data, data.cdc.gov); public domain in the United States.
snapshots.derivation: Rows of NNDSS Weekly Data for Massachusetts, New England, and U.S. residents (reporting-area names in either letter case), MMWR years 2022-2026, weeks 36, 37, 38, 39, 40, 41, 42, 43, 52, 53 (the latest published week for Massachusetts, the 7 weeks before it, and year-end weeks 52 and 53). Kept: current-week count (m1) and cumulative year-to-date count (m3) for every row, and the previous year's cumulative count (m4) for 2022 rows only. Counts are stored as published; CDC flags are kept as codes. Built by `cargo xtask build-surveillance-snapshots`.
caveats: Provisional counts as published each week; CDC revises them, and finalized annual counts (CDC Stacks annual tables) can differ.
Covers only the latest week in the snapshot; other weeks need the live dataset.

snapshots.title: CDC respiratory virus surveillance for Massachusetts (NHSN, NSSP, NREVSS, ARI level)
snapshots.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
snapshots.license: U.S. federal government work (CDC open data, data.cdc.gov); public domain in the United States.
snapshots.derivation: The last 13 weeks of rows returned by data.cdc.gov for NHSN Weekly Hospital Respiratory Admission Levels and Rates (vdzy-6i9v; MA and USA), NSSP ED visit trajectories (rdmq-nq56; Massachusetts and United States, state level), NREVSS percent positivity for SARS-CoV-2 (gvsb-yw6g) and RSV (3cxc-4k8q) for HHS Region 1 and the nation, national percent of tests positive (seuz-s2cv), and the acute respiratory illness activity level by state (f3zz-zga5), with the columns the tool uses. Built by `cargo xtask build-surveillance-snapshots`.
caveats: Snapshot of recent weeks only; data are provisional and CDC revises them.

snapshots.title: CDC wastewater viral activity levels for Massachusetts sampling sites (NWSS)
snapshots.license: U.S. federal government work (CDC open data, data.cdc.gov); public domain in the United States.
snapshots.derivation: The last 13 weeks of site-level wastewater viral activity levels (WVAL) for SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, and RSV at Massachusetts sites (atcp-73re), as returned by data.cdc.gov. Built by `cargo xtask build-surveillance-snapshots`.
caveats: CDC identifies sites only by an arbitrary number, counties served, and population served.

snapshots.title: MWRA Deer Island wastewater SARS-CoV-2 (Biobot), final 12 months
snapshots.publisher: Massachusetts Water Resources Authority (MWRA); testing by Biobot Analytics
snapshots.license: Public data published by MWRA, a Massachusetts public authority.
snapshots.derivation: Sample date, Southern and Northern system SARS-CoV-2 RNA (copies/mL), and their 7-day averages for 2025-07-27 to 2026-07-27, read from MWRA's data PDF with `pdftotext -tsv` and assigned to columns by x position (boundaries [89.0, 138.5, 187.1, 235.7, 284.3] points, checked against the page-1 header). The codes 'nd' (also printed 'ND') and 'NS' are kept as printed; the PDF has no legend for them. Confidence intervals and variant results are not kept. Built by `cargo xtask build-surveillance-snapshots`.
caveats: MWRA's Biobot testing ended with samples collected through 2026-07-27; DPH is moving Deer Island testing to its own program and dashboard.
Values are as transcribed from a PDF table; check the PDF before quoting a single value.

snapshots.title: DPH Guide to Surveillance, Reporting and Control (disease chapters) and DPH infectious disease fact sheets (text corpus)
snapshots.source_vintage: 25 guide chapters (2016–2023, dates in the corpus) and 66 DPH web pages
snapshots.license: Massachusetts state government publications (public records); quoted with citation.
snapshots.derivation: Downloaded from mass.gov; DOCX and RTF chapters and HTML page bodies converted to plain text and split into sections (chapter sections and lettered subsections; page headings). Built by `cargo xtask build-guide-corpus`.
caveats: Most guide chapters are dated 2016–2018 (a few 2022–2023); DPH guidance for some diseases (for example respiratory viruses) has changed since. Check the date of each passage and confirm current practice with DPH.
Text was extracted automatically from DOCX, RTF, and web pages: tables are flattened to lines with ' | ' between cells, and images (including flowcharts) are not included.
Not included: Streptococcus pneumoniae - Invasive Disease (2016) (https://www.mass.gov/doc/streptococcus-pneumoniae-invasive-disease-2016/download): unsupported format (not DOCX or RTF).

snapshots.title: Number of Opioid-Related Overdose Deaths, All Intents by City/Town, 2015-2022
snapshots.publisher: Massachusetts Department of Public Health (Registry of Vital Records and Statistics)
snapshots.license: Public report of the Massachusetts Department of Public Health.
snapshots.derivation: Table 1 (city/town of residence, Massachusetts residents) and Table 2 (city/town of death occurrence) transcribed from `pdftotext -layout` output: one row per basis and town with yearly counts 2015-2022, plus the Unknown, Out of Massachusetts, and Total rows. The builder checks that each table's rows sum to the published totals and that 351 towns are present. DPH spellings are kept (Manchester, North Attleboro). Builder: xtask/scripts/build_overdose_towns.py.
caveats: This June 2023 table is the latest town-level table DPH published as a document; later town data (through 2025) are only on DPH's BSAS dashboard (Community Profile).
2020-2022 counts were preliminary when posted; DPH's later reports use an updated 'opioid-involved' method, so their counts differ slightly from this table. Do not mix the two series.
Counts are as published by DPH, including small numbers.

snapshots.title: VSRR provisional drug overdose death counts: Massachusetts, U.S., and Massachusetts counties
snapshots.publisher: CDC, National Center for Health Statistics (National Vital Statistics System)
snapshots.source_vintage: 12 month-ending periods through May 2026 (state, rows updated 2026-10-14) and March 2026 (counties, data as of 2026-10-04)
snapshots.license: U.S. federal government work (CDC open data, data.cdc.gov); public domain in the United States.
snapshots.derivation: State file: rows of xkb8-kh2a for state MA and US from January 2019 for nine indicators (all drug overdose deaths; opioids; synthetic opioids other than methadone; heroin; natural and semi-synthetic opioids; methadone; cocaine; psychostimulants; percent with drugs specified), keeping reported and predicted values, percent complete, percent pending investigation, and the footnote symbol. County file: rows of gb4e-yj24 for the 14 Massachusetts counties from January 2020, keeping the 12 month-ending count (blank when NCHS suppressed a count of 1-9), footnote, urban-rural code, percent pending, and data date. Builder: xtask/scripts/build_overdose_vsrr.py (Python 3 and curl).
caveats: Provisional counts are incomplete and are revised monthly; predicted values adjust for reporting delays.
State counts are by the jurisdiction where the death occurred; county counts are by county of residence.
County counts of 1-9 are suppressed by NCHS.
